content.text:
The pattern matches a single phase, CaZrGeO5 (mp-644295).

I simulated only two candidates, the two triclinic ones (CaZrGeO5 and Rb4CuSi2O7). I picked them because the observed pattern has many peaks starting near 17°. I compared peak positions and heights by eye against the simulated CaZrGeO5 pattern. The other seven candidates were not simulated or checked.

- **Peaks that line up:** the triplet at about 16.8–17.9°, and the weak peaks near 20.7°, 22.0–22.5° and 24°. Also the doublet at about 26.9–27.4°, the strongest peak near 28.5°, and the broad cluster at about 32.7–34°. Weaker peaks at higher angles fall in the right places too.
- **Relative intensities:** the 100 peak and the ~77 peak in the doublet are close to the simulated values. So are the heights of the 32.7–34° cluster.
- **Leftover peaks:** I saw none that CaZrGeO5 fails to explain, so there is no sign of a second phase.

{"present": ["mp-644295"], "confidence": 0.9, "note": "The observed peak positions and relative intensities match the simulated CaZrGeO5 pattern from 16.8 to 80 degrees, with no unexplained peaks, so a single phase is indicated."}
